title: Senior Product Marketing Manager
description:
We're looking for a Senior Product Marketing Manager to own positioning, messaging and go-to-market across our model APIs, serverless compute and dedicated capacity. You'll turn our technical capabilities into clear propositions that help customers understand what to use, why it matters and how to get started.

This is a hands-on role. You'll interview customers, collaborate with engineers, create product marketing content and enable Sales, working closely with Product, Engineering, Growth and Ecosystem teams.

📍 Location: United States (Remote) — with some overlap with European working hours required.

What you’ll do

• Own positioning and messaging across model APIs, serverless and dedicated compute, developing differentiated value propositions for priority segments and use cases.

• Translate technical capabilities into customer value, highlighting cost, performance, reliability and time to deployment, backed by clear evidence.

• Conduct customer and competitive research to understand workloads, buying criteria, objections, alternatives and market opportunities.

• Lead go-to-market and product launches, coordinating messaging, demos, product pages and customer communications across teams.

• Create compelling product marketing content, including product pages, use-case narratives, presentations, competitive comparisons and customer stories.

• Enable Sales with pitch materials, discovery guidance and objection-handling resources.

• Partner with Growth and Ecosystem on campaigns that drive trial, adoption and expansion.

• Measure and optimize impact on qualified demand, conversion and product usage to inform priorities.

Requirements

• Senior-level product marketing experience in technical B2B, such as APIs, developer platforms, cloud services or infrastructure products.

• Proven ability to simplify and differentiate complex technical products through clear positioning and messaging.

• Experience leading cross-functional product launches, coordinating efforts across multiple teams.

• Excellent writing skills, with examples of product pages, presentations or launch materials you've created yourself.

• Technical understanding of AI inference, GPU compute and deployment models, sufficient to communicate their value to customers.

• Strong commercial mindset, with the ability to work with funnel metrics and product usage data.

• Customer research skills, with the ability to turn interviews and market insights into actionable decisions.

• Ability to collaborate with and influence cross-functional teams, particularly Product, Engineering and Sales.

Nice to Have

• Experience in AI infrastructure or GPU cloud.

• Familiarity with usage-based pricing models.

• Experience marketing to both developers and enterprise buyers.

Benefits

We’re a remote-first collective, meeting in person twice a year to plan, brainstorm, celebrate wins, and enjoy some face-to-face time. We have core hours for cooperative working and calls, but outside of that your calendar is yours. Work the hours that let you perform at your peak while also building a healthy life.

Our release cycles are fast and intense, but they’re followed by real downtime. After big pushes we expect the team to unplug, recharge, and come back ready & stronger than ever for the next leap.

• Generous paid time off – vacation, sick days, public holidays

• Meaningful stock options – share in the upside you create

• Flexible hours – own your schedule outside core collaboration blocks

• Family leave – paid maternity, paternity, and caregiver time

• Company retreats – twice-yearly gatherings in inspiring locations

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer who thrives on turning ambitious ideas into production systems that delight developers and deliver real business impact.

You’ll work across the stack, from backend APIs and orchestration to SDKs, dashboards, and developer tools. You’ll take ownership from start to finish, understanding user needs, designing elegant solutions, and delivering outcomes that make building with AI faster, simpler, and more creative.

You’ll collaborate across the company to build systems that are robust, performant, and a joy to work on. This role combines technical depth, product intuition, and leadership, making it ideal for engineers who want to shape both how things are built and why they matter.

Is this role a fit for you?

You are motivated by impact. You thrive on transforming complex AI systems into products that developers love to use. You think holistically about architecture, user experience, and business outcomes, and you take pride in delivering systems that are both elegant and dependable.

You are equally comfortable designing APIs, building scalable backend services, and improving developer-facing experiences. You set a high bar for quality, mentor others to reach it, and drive alignment between product ambition and technical reality.

What this role could entail

• Lead the design and implementation of core systems powering Runware’s AI platform

• Build and evolve backend APIs, SDKs, and developer tools that make AI integration seamless

• Integrate and optimise image and video models while supporting new modalities such as audio and custom LLMs

• Architect scalable, reliable systems for inference orchestration and workload optimisation

• Partner with platform and infrastructure teams to drive performance, reliability, and observability improvements

• Shape technical direction through architectural discussions and long-term planning

• Mentor engineers through code and design reviews, fostering technical excellence and growth

• Contribute to documentation, tooling, and SDKs that enhance the overall developer experience

• Drive initiatives that improve how we build, deploy, and maintain our platform

Requirements

• Deep experience building distributed and high-performance systems

• Strong programming skills in PHP or Go

• Proven track record of designing and delivering scalable backend systems and APIs

• Understanding of asynchronous workloads, queues, and streaming data

• Experience working with cloud and bare-metal infrastructure

• Excellent grasp of system design, performance optimisation, and scalability principles

• Clear communicator who leads technical projects and collaborates effectively across teams

• Passionate about mentoring others and raising engineering standards

• Proactive problem-solver who balances short-term progress with long-term vision

• European time zone

Benefits

We’re a remote-first collective, meeting in person twice a year to plan, brainstorm, celebrate wins, and enjoy some face-to-face time. We have core hours for cooperative working and calls, but outside of that your calendar is yours. Work the hours that let you perform at your peak while also building a healthy life.

We move quickly and hold a high bar, but we also believe sustainable performance matters. After major releases and milestones, we create space for the team to properly unplug, recharge and come back with the energy to tackle what's next.

• Generous paid time off – vacation, sick days, public holidays

• Meaningful stock options – share in the upside you create

• Remote-first setup – work from home anywhere we can employ you

• Flexible hours – own your schedule outside core collaboration blocks

• Family leave – paid maternity, paternity, and caregiver time

• Company retreats – twice-yearly gatherings in inspiring locations

title: Staff Software Engineer - Serverless
description:
We’re looking for a Staff/Senior Software Engineer to technically lead and build Runware’s serverless platform. You’ll be part of a small team working closely with senior leadership to bring a new product line to market.

Runware is evolving beyond model APIs into a platform where developers can deploy models and run AI workloads without managing GPUs, servers or infrastructure. You’ll build the software layer that connects our proprietary high-performance sonic inference engine and turns complex infrastructure into a compelling developer experience.

This is a role for someone who enjoys technical leadership, hard platform problems and clean, simple systems. Your work will help enterprises, model labs and developers move from idea to production faster, then scale without needing to build and operate the infrastructure themselves.

What you’ll do

• Build the core systems behind Runware’s serverless platform, including workload execution, routing, scheduling, isolation and scaling leveraging our inference engine

• Make it simple for developers to deploy models and run AI workloads without managing GPUs, servers, queues or infrastructure through a simple SDK interface

• Design and improve the control plane for serverless execution, including APIs, workers, lifecycle management, retries and failure handling

• Work closely with our infrastructure and ML teams to improve workload startup time, GPU utilisation, model warm-up, caching and placement

• Build observability that makes serverless workloads easy to monitor, debug and operate at scale globally

• Lead the technical design, mentor other engineers and help define the engineering standards for a new product area

Requirements

• Strong experience as a Staff Engineer, Senior Software Engineer, Backend Engineer, Platform Engineer or similar

• Experience building backend services, distributed systems, developer platforms or workload orchestration systems

• Strong understanding of async processing, queues, scheduling, retries, back pressure and failure handling

• Comfortable working across APIs, control planes, workers, databases and observability systems

• Strong engineering fundamentals in one or more backend languages ideally Go

• Good judgement around trade-offs between reliability, latency, scale, cost and developer experience

• Clear communication, strong ownership and the ability to lead technical direction in a fast-moving environment

Nice to have

• Experience building serverless platforms, job execution systems, container platforms or compute orchestration systems

• Experience with GPU-backed workloads, AI/ML inference, model serving, batch processing or high-performance compute

• Familiarity with technologies such as vLLM, TensorRT, Triton, Kubernetes, Nomad or Knative

• Experience improving workload performance through batching, autoscaling, model warm-up, caching, request routing or queue management

• Experience with multi-tenant isolation, sandboxing, quotas, rate limits, resource accounting or usage-based billing

Benefits

title: AI Factory Network Architect
description:
About Runware

Runware is the AI inference platform that builds and runs its own infrastructure, end to end. Our Sonic Inference Engine has served more than 20 billion requests for over 1 million developers and 500 million end users, with 400,000+ models behind a single integration, at up to 10x lower cost per token than traditional providers.

We are now building the AI Factory that runs it. The Sonic Inference Pod packs 1 MW of custom-designed compute into a 20-foot container with closed-loop, water-free cooling, sited wherever power exists. Pods are live in the US and Europe, and we are scaling to dozens of pods and tens of thousands of GPUs, all operated as one distributed fabric that reroutes traffic the moment a pod goes offline (announcement).

The network is what turns those pods into a supercomputer. That is the job.

The role

As AI Factory Network Architect, you will own the network architecture of Runware's AI supercomputer, from the NVLink domain inside a server to the optical links between pods on two continents. You will set the design, build the first systems with your own hands, and grow the team that runs them.

This is a hands-on leadership role, not a slide-deck role. You will specify the fabrics, validate them on real hardware, debug the first congestion collapse at 3 a.m., and then write the standard so it never happens again. You will work directly with our hardware, platform, and inference engineering teams, with NVIDIA and our optical and switching vendors, and with the site teams deploying pods.

Success means inference traffic flows across tens of thousands of GPUs at line rate, pods join the fabric in days rather than weeks, and a failure anywhere in the network is invisible to the developer calling our API.

What you'll do

• Own the end-to-end network architecture for the AI Factory: the scale-up fabric (NVLink and NVSwitch domains), the scale-out fabric (InfiniBand and RoCE), the storage and management networks, and the pod-to-pod and inter-site backbone.

• Design the optical layer: transceiver and cable selection, co-packaged and linear-drive optics evaluation, DWDM for pod-to-pod and metro links, and the link budgets and reliability targets behind them.

• Define the reference network design for the Sonic Inference Pod so every new pod ships with a validated, repeatable fabric and joins the global network in days.

• Build and bring up the first fabrics yourself: rail-optimized topologies, subnet manager and routing configuration, adaptive routing, congestion control, QoS, and GPUDirect RDMA tuning, measured against inference throughput and tail latency rather than synthetic benchmarks.

• Work with the inference engine team so the Sonic Inference Engine's traffic patterns, from tensor- and pipeline-parallel collectives to KV-cache transfer and multi-node serving, drive topology and buffer decisions, not the other way round.

• Run capacity planning and the vendor roadmap with NVIDIA, switch and optics suppliers, and carriers; negotiate technical specifications and lead evaluations of new fabric generations.

• Set the operating standard: telemetry, link-health monitoring, failure-domain design, automated fault isolation, and runbooks that let a small team operate tens of thousands of ports.

• Hire and lead a team of network engineers as the footprint grows, and act as the final technical escalation for fabric incidents across all sites.

Requirements

What we're looking for

• 15+ years designing, building, and operating high-performance networks, with a significant part of that in HPC or AI supercomputers at the scale of thousands of GPUs or more.

• Deep, hands-on InfiniBand experience: fabric design, subnet management, routing engines, adaptive routing, congestion control, and performance debugging at the port and queue-pair level.

• Working knowledge of NVLink and NVSwitch domains and how scale-up and scale-out fabrics interact for multi-GPU and multi-node inference and training.

• Optical networking depth: transceivers and cabling at 400G and 800G, link budgets, DWDM and coherent optics for inter-site links, and the operational realities of optics at scale (failure rates, cleaning, inventory).

• Hands-on RDMA experience across InfiniBand and RoCE, including GPUDirect, NCCL and collective behaviour, PFC and ECN tuning, and the trade-offs between the two.

• A track record of leading network teams through greenfield builds and production incidents, and of being the person engineers call when the fabric is doing something nobody understands.

• Comfort automating everything: Python or Go, infrastructure as code, and telemetry pipelines rather than CLI sessions.

• Clear writing and the ability to turn a design into a document that a site team on another continent can execute from.

• Willingness to travel to pod sites in the US and Europe for bring-up and major changes.

Strong differentiators

• Experience with NVIDIA Spectrum-X, Quantum-X800, or Blackwell-generation NVLink systems, or the equivalent from a hyperscaler's in-house stack.

• Hands-on time with co-packaged optics, linear-drive pluggables, or photonic switching evaluations.

• Experience designing networks for modular or containerized data centers, edge sites, or deployments with constrained power and space.

• Background in inference-specific traffic patterns: disaggregated prefill and decode, KV-cache transfer, and multi-tenant serving across a shared fabric.

• Contributions to SONiC, OpenFabrics, UEC, or similar open networking efforts.

• Experience with sovereign or data-residency network designs, including inter-site encryption and segmentation.

• Prior work at a GPU cloud, hyperscaler, national lab, or AI lab building its own supercomputer.

Benefits

Why Runware

You will design the network for an AI supercomputer that is being built right now, with the budget, the hardware, and the mandate to do it properly. Few network architects get to own a fabric from the first pod to the global backbone, with a direct line to the people deciding what the next pod looks like.

We're a remote-first collective, meeting in person twice a year to plan, brainstorm, celebrate wins, and enjoy some face-to-face time. We have core hours for cooperative working and calls, but outside of that your calendar is yours. Work the hours that let you perform at your peak while also building a healthy life.

Our release cycles are fast and intense, but they're followed by real downtime. After big pushes we expect the team to unplug, recharge, and come back ready and stronger than ever for the next leap.

• Generous paid time off: vacation, sick days, public holidays

• Meaningful stock options: share in the upside you create

• Flexible hours: own your schedule outside core collaboration blocks

• Family leave: paid maternity, paternity, and caregiver time

• Company retreats: twice-yearly gatherings in inspiring locations

title: Head of Infrastructure Operations
description:
About Runware

Runware is the AI inference platform that builds and operates its own infrastructure, end to end. One API gives developers access to image, video, audio, 3D and language models, and our Sonic Inference Engine runs them on hardware we designed ourselves: custom servers, custom boards and a closed-loop, water-free cooling system, packed into Sonic Inference Pods — roughly 1 MW of liquid-cooled GPU compute in a 20-foot container that can be sited wherever power is cheap and available.

This is why infrastructure at Runware is the product, not a cost center. Our edge is that we run inference 30–90% cheaper per GPU-hour than our peers, and that edge is earned in the data center: in how fast we can stand up a new site, how tightly we run our fleet, and how little downtime our customers ever see. More than 20 billion requests have run through the platform for over a million developers, with customers such as Wix, Quora, Freepik and Higgsfield building production applications on top of it.

We raised a $50M Series A led by Dawn Capital, with Comcast Ventures, Speedinvest, Insight Partners and a16z speedrun participating, and we are now building out a global network of pods across the US and Europe. We need someone to own how that network is operated.

The role

As Head of Infrastructure Operations, you'll own the physical and operational backbone of Runware: the servers, storage and networking across every site we run, and the team that keeps them running. You'll take us from a handful of pods to a global fleet, and you'll decide how that fleet is built, provisioned, monitored, maintained and scaled.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You'll set the operating model and hire the team, but you'll also be in the terminal, in the rack and in the incident channel when it matters. The people who do best here are senior operators who never stopped being engineers, who are already using AI tools to multiply their own output, and who know what a high-performance infrastructure team looks like because they've built one before.

You'll report to Risto Haukioja, Head of AI Infrastructure and work closely with the hardware, platform and inference engineering teams, and with our data center, power and hardware partners.

What you'll do

• Build and run global infrastructure operations across our pod sites in the US and Europe: site bring-up, rack and stack, cabling, power and cooling integration, burn-in and acceptance, through to steady-state operations and decommissioning.

• Own the server, storage and network layers of the fleet end to end: Linux fleet management, bare-metal provisioning and imaging, firmware and driver lifecycle, high-throughput storage for model weights and caches, and the data center and inter-site networks that tie it together.

• Define how a new site goes live, then make it faster every time. Turn pod deployment into a repeatable, documented, largely automated playbook so that standing up the next 1 MW is a routine, not a project.

• Set and hit reliability targets. Own capacity planning, monitoring, alerting, on-call, incident response and post-incident reviews, and drive the GPU, node and network failure rates down over time.

• Hire, lead and develop a high-performance team of data center, systems and network engineers across time zones, and set the bar for how that team operates.

• Manage colocation, power, connectivity and hardware vendors and partners, including capacity contracts, lead times, spares and RMA flows, and site-level budgets.

• Partner with hardware and platform engineering so that what we design is operable at scale, and feed what you learn in the field back into the next generation of servers and pods.

• Use AI to accelerate the work: automate runbooks, triage and tooling with LLM-based agents, and expect your team to do the same, so that a small team can run a very large fleet.

• Own the operational side of security and compliance for our physical infrastructure: access control, hardening, asset tracking and audit readiness, including data residency requirements for in-country deployments.

Requirements

What we're looking for

• 15+ years in infrastructure engineering and operations, with at least several of those leading the function at a company that runs its own hardware at scale.

• A track record of building infrastructure operations across multiple sites, regions or countries, not just operating what someone else built. You've opened data centers, pods or colocation footprints and know what goes wrong between the plan and the first production workload.

• Deep, current, hands-on Linux expertise: kernel and driver behaviour, performance tuning, bare-metal provisioning, configuration management and fleet automation. You can still debug a misbehaving node at 2 a.m. and you'd rather fix the root cause than restart it.

• Strong storage fundamentals: NVMe, distributed and parallel file systems, object storage, and designing for the throughput and IOPS that model loading and caching demand.

• Strong networking fundamentals: L2/L3 design, BGP, data center fabrics, high-bandwidth interconnects and the debugging skills to find a flapping link or a misconfigured switch quickly.

• Experience running high-performance teams: you've hired, led and retained strong engineers, set clear standards, and built an on-call and incident culture that people are proud of rather than burned out by.

• You use AI to accelerate your own output every day, for scripting, runbooks, analysis, documentation and debugging, and you have a clear view of how a small team armed with these tools should operate differently from a traditional ops org.

• Comfortable owning outcomes in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment, making decisions with incomplete information and being accountable for uptime, cost and delivery.

• Able to travel to sites in the US and Europe as needed.

Nice to have

• Experience operating large GPU fleets for AI training or inference, including NVIDIA driver, Fabric Manager and NCCL stacks, and GPU health and failure management at scale.

• Hands-on experience with RDMA fabrics (InfiniBand or RoCE), 400G+ Ethernet and the tooling to monitor them.

• Experience with liquid-cooled, high-density or modular and containerized data center designs, and with power and cooling integration at the site level.

• Familiarity with the hardware supply chain: server ODMs, component lead times, inventory and spares strategy, and RMA economics.

• A strong automation stack background: Ansible, Terraform, PXE and image pipelines, IPMI and Redfish, and observability with Prometheus and Grafana or similar.

• Experience with Kubernetes or Slurm on bare metal.

• Experience building or running infrastructure to meet data residency, sovereignty or compliance requirements across jurisdictions.

Benefits

What we offer

• A rare mandate: build global AI infrastructure operations from the ground up, at a company whose business depends on doing it better than anyone else, with the budget and backing to match.

• Meaningful stock options.

• We're a remote-first collective, meeting in person twice a year to plan, brainstorm and celebrate wins. We keep core hours for collaboration and calls; outside those, you set your own schedule.

• Our release cycles are fast and intense, and they're followed by real downtime. We expect you to take it.

• Generous paid time off, including vacation, sick days and public holidays.

• Paid maternity, paternity and caregiver leave.

• Twice-yearly company retreats in inspiring locations.

title: Network Architect
description:
About Runware

Runware is the AI inference platform that builds and operates its own infrastructure, end to end. One API gives developers access to image, video, audio, 3D and language models, and our Sonic Inference Engine runs them on hardware we designed ourselves: custom servers, custom boards and a closed-loop, water-free cooling system, packed into Sonic Inference Pods — roughly 1 MW of liquid-cooled GPU compute in a 20-foot container that can be sited wherever power is cheap and available.

This is why infrastructure at Runware is the product, not a cost center. Our edge is that we run inference 30–90% cheaper per GPU-hour than our peers, and that edge is earned in the data center: in how fast we can stand up a new site, how tightly we run our fleet, and how little downtime our customers ever see. More than 20 billion requests have run through the platform for over a million developers, with customers such as Wix, Quora, Freepik and Higgsfield building production applications on top of it.

We raised a $50M Series A led by Dawn Capital, with Comcast Ventures, Speedinvest, Insight Partners and a16z speedrun participating, and we are now building out a global network of pods across the US and Europe. We need someone to own how that network is operated.

The Role

As Network Architect, you'll own the design, build, and operation of the network that moves every inference request through Runware: the GPU cluster fabric inside our data centers, the backbone and edge that deliver results to customers, and the cloud and hybrid connectivity that ties partner capacity into one platform. Runware's product is latency. The network is where a large share of that latency, and of our cost per request, is decided, and today there is no single owner for it. You'll be that owner.

This is a senior, hands-on architecture role with significant authority and no direct reports to start. You'll report to Risto Haukioja, Head of AI Infrastructure. You'll set the network strategy, design and build the systems yourself, define how they are operated and capacity-planned, and lead through design authority across Infrastructure, Platform, and ML Engineering. You've run high-performance teams before, and you'll shape the standards and hiring plan for network engineering as the footprint grows. We expect you to use AI tooling as a core part of how you work, so that one architect can produce what a small team used to.

What you'll do

• Own the network architecture end to end. Define the target architecture and multi-year roadmap for Runware's data center fabric, backbone and edge, and cloud and hybrid connectivity, and make the design decisions that trade off latency, throughput, cost, and resilience.

• Design and build the GPU cluster fabric. Architect spine-leaf fabrics for multi-node inference and training: 400G/800G Ethernet, RoCEv2 and InfiniBand, lossless transport, congestion control, and topology choices that keep east-west traffic from becoming the bottleneck.

• Deliver inference to customers fast and reliably. Own the backbone and edge: multi-region interconnect, transit and peering strategy, anycast and traffic steering, DDoS and edge security posture, and the path that gets every response to the customer with as few milliseconds as possible.

• Connect cloud, bare metal, and partner capacity into one platform. Design VPC, VPN, and private interconnect across hyperscalers, bare-metal providers, and colocation sites so new capacity can be brought online quickly and operated consistently.

• Build network operations, not just networks. Define how the network is monitored, changed, and repaired: telemetry and observability, change management, incident runbooks, and on-call practices that hold up at scale. Stand up what doesn't exist yet.

• Run capacity planning. Build the models that forecast bandwidth, port, and interconnect needs from product growth, and turn them into procurement and build plans with lead times that match the business, not the other way round.

• Automate the network. Treat network configuration as code: IaC, intent-based provisioning, automated validation and rollback, and telemetry-driven remediation, so the network can grow without a proportional growth in people.

• Accelerate your own output with AI. Use AI tools throughout your work (design exploration, configuration generation, log and telemetry analysis, documentation, automation code) and set the standard for how the wider infrastructure team does the same.

• Lead through design authority. Set network standards, review designs across Infrastructure, Platform, and ML Engineering, mentor engineers, and define the hiring plan and operating model for network engineering as the footprint grows.

• Own vendor and carrier relationships. Evaluate and select hardware, optics, carriers, and interconnect partners, and negotiate for performance and cost.

Requirements

• 15+ years in network engineering and architecture, including at least 5 years as the design authority for large-scale production networks at a cloud provider, hyperscaler, CDN, HPC/AI infrastructure company, or carrier.

• Hands-on. You still design, configure, and troubleshoot networks yourself, and you've built data center, backbone, and cloud networks from the ground up, not just inherited them.

• Deep, current expertise in modern data center networking: spine-leaf Clos fabrics, EVPN/VXLAN, BGP at scale, 400G/800G Ethernet, RoCEv2 and lossless Ethernet (PFC, ECN, DCQCN), and InfiniBand for GPU clusters.

• Strong backbone and edge experience: multi-region interconnect, transit and peering, anycast, traffic engineering, and DDoS mitigation, with a track record of measurably reducing customer-facing latency.

• Cloud and hybrid networking across at least two hyperscalers plus bare-metal or colocation environments: VPC design, private interconnect (Direct Connect, ExpressRoute, Cloud Interconnect or equivalent), and VPN at scale.

• Experience designing and running network operations: observability, change management, incident response, and on-call, with the judgement to know what to build first when starting from little.

• Proven capacity planning: you've built forecasting models that turned product growth into bandwidth, port, and interconnect plans, and you've run the procurement cycles that followed.

• Network automation as a working practice, not an aspiration: Python or Go, IaC for network config, CI-style validation, and streaming telemetry.

• You use AI to accelerate your own output. You can show how AI tooling is part of how you design, write configuration and automation code, analyse telemetry, and document, and you expect it to multiply what you ship.

• Experience leading high-performance engineering teams: you've hired, set standards, and run teams that delivered under pressure, and you lead well through influence when you have no direct reports.

• Strong ownership and comfort in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment where you identify the problems, create clarity, and drive the work to done.

• Based in, or with full working overlap with, US Pacific time.

Strong Differentiators

• Experience networking large GPU clusters for AI inference or training (NVIDIA Spectrum-X, Quantum InfiniBand, NCCL tuning, GPUDirect RDMA), and an opinion on Ethernet versus InfiniBand backed by production numbers.

• Hands-on with modern network operating systems and disaggregated hardware: SONiC, Cumulus, Arista EOS, Junos, or NVIDIA Cumulus/Spectrum platforms.

title: Senior Security Engineer
description:
About Runware

Runware is the AI inference platform that builds and runs its own infrastructure, end to end. Our Sonic Inference Engine has served more than 20 billion requests for over 1 million developers and 500 million end users, with 400,000+ models behind a single integration, at up to 10x lower cost per token than traditional providers.

The Sonic Inference Pod packs 1 MW of custom-designed compute into a 20-foot container with closed-loop, water-free cooling, sited wherever power exists. Pods are live in the US and Europe, and we are scaling to dozens of pods and tens of thousands of GPUs, all operated as one distributed fabric that reroutes traffic the moment a pod goes offline (announcement).

Every one of those pods holds customer models, customer data and millions of dollars of GPUs, sometimes inside a customer's own perimeter or a sovereign jurisdiction. Keeping all of it secure without slowing anyone down is the job.

The role

As Senior Security Engineer, you will own the security of Runware's AI supercomputer: the bare-metal GPU fleet, the Sonic Inference Pods it lives in, the managed Kubernetes clusters we hand to customers, and the control plane that ties it all together across the US and Europe. You will design the controls, build the first version with your own hands, and set the standard for how security is run across every pod.

This is a hands-on senior individual-contributor role. You will threat-model a new pod before it ships, harden the image that every GPU node boots from, prove to an enterprise customer's security team that their model weights never leave their tenant, and when something goes wrong, lead the response and fix the root cause so it never happens again. You will work directly with our CISO, with the inference engine, platform and hardware teams, and with the site teams deploying pods.

Success means a customer workload on a shared pod is isolated as strongly as on a dedicated one, no human has a standing login to a production node, every change to the fleet is reviewed, signed and auditable, and an enterprise security review takes days instead of months.

What you'll do

• Own the security architecture of the fleet: host hardening for bare-metal GPU nodes, immutable images and a signed build pipeline, boot integrity, and the identity, secrets and access model for humans and services across every pod.

• Secure multi-tenancy on shared infrastructure. Design and verify isolation between customer workloads at the network, Kubernetes, host and GPU layers, and produce the evidence that proves it holds.

• Secure the managed Kubernetes offering: cluster hardening, admission control, RBAC, supply-chain controls for images, and a clean, auditable handover of clusters to customers.

• Build security visibility across the fleet: logging, detection, alerting and audit trails from firmware to API, wired into the fleet dashboards and on-call so that an anomaly on one node in one pod is seen within minutes.

• Lead security reviews and threat models for new pods, sites, servers and platform features, with a focus on real-world risk rather than checklists.

• Run incident response for the infrastructure: investigation, containment, recovery and post-incident learning, as part of the on-call rotation.

• Own vulnerability management for the fleet: firmware, kernel, drivers, GPU stack and container images across thousands of nodes, with a patch cadence you can defend to a customer.

• Answer enterprise customers' security due diligence with engineering evidence, and partner with the CISO on the SOC 2 and ISO 27001 controls that touch the infrastructure.

• Design for sovereign and on-premise deployments: data residency, in-country key management, and physical and remote-access controls for a pod sitting on a customer's site.

• Use AI to accelerate the work: automate evidence collection, log triage, configuration audits and runbooks with LLM-based agents, so that a very small team can secure a very large fleet.

Requirements

What we're looking for

• 8+ years in security or infrastructure engineering, with several of those securing production infrastructure at a company that runs its own hardware at scale.

• A track record of building security controls, not just auditing them. You have taken a hardening standard, an access model or a detection pipeline from design to running across a fleet, and you know what breaks between the two.

• Deep, current, hands-on Linux security expertise: kernel hardening, namespaces and cgroups, seccomp, eBPF, secure and measured boot, TPM-based attestation, and the tooling to see exactly what a process did.

• Strong Kubernetes security: RBAC, admission control and policy engines, network policy, runtime security, image signing and SBOMs, and the ways a container escapes.

• Fluent in network security on real hardware: segmentation and VLAN or VXLAN isolation, firewalls, out-of-band management networks, and the risks that live in BMC, IPMI and switch management planes.

• Experience with identity, secrets and PKI at scale: short-lived credentials, workload identity, hardware-backed keys, and removing standing access without slowing engineers down.

Nice to have

title: Senior Storage Engineer
description:

The role

You will design the data path, build the first version with your own hands, and set the standard for how storage is run across every pod.

This is a hands-on senior individual-contributor role. You will specify the systems, benchmark them on real hardware, find the reason a 70 GB checkpoint took four minutes to load instead of twenty seconds, and then fix it at the root so it never happens again. You will work directly with our inference engine, platform and hardware teams, with our storage and NVMe vendors, and with the site teams deploying pods.

Success means a cold model loads onto a GPU anywhere in the fleet in seconds, a new pod has its working set warm before it takes traffic, and a disk, node or whole site failing is invisible to the developer calling our API.

What you'll do

• Design and build the model distribution path. Decide how weights get from the source of truth to a pod, how they are chunked, deduplicated, prefetched and pinned, and how a new pod warms its working set before it takes production traffic.

• Drive model load latency down and keep it down. Profile the full path from disk to GPU memory, including the kernel, file system, NVMe-oF or RDMA transport, GPUDirect Storage and the inference engine's loader, and remove the bottleneck wherever it sits.

• Select, benchmark and operate the storage systems themselves: parallel and distributed file systems, object storage, NVMe drives and enclosures, and the software that manages them. Validate every choice on our hardware before it ships to a pod.

• Set and hit reliability and durability targets. Own capacity planning, monitoring, alerting, drive health and failure prediction, rebuild behaviour, backup and recovery, and on-call for the storage layer.

• Make storage a routine part of pod bring-up: a documented, automated playbook so that the storage tier of the next 1 MW pod is provisioned, validated and warm in hours, not weeks.

• Strong understanding of NVMe, NVMe-oF, RDMA transports and the networking that storage rides on. You can tell a saturated PCIe link from a slow drive from a misconfigured switch.

title: Principal Engineer, Model Performance
description:

You will set the performance roadmap, build the hardest pieces with your own hands, and build and lead the Model Performance team as it grows around you.

This is a principal-level role for someone who has led inference performance work at the frontier and still writes the kernel. You will decide where the next 2x comes from on a given model and hardware generation, whether that is a fused attention kernel, a better quantization recipe, speculative decoding, a smarter batching policy or a different parallelism layout, and then make it land in production on real traffic. You will work directly with the Sonic Inference Engine team, the infrastructure and hardware teams, and with NVIDIA and the open-source engine communities, and you will hire, mentor and lead the engineers who do this work alongside you.

Success means Runware serves a new open model at the Pareto frontier of latency and cost within days of its weights being released, our cost per request keeps falling with every hardware generation, and the team you have built can do this without you in the loop.

What you'll do

• Own inference performance end to end for the fleet: the kernels, the serving engines, the model-level optimizations and the benchmarks that prove them, across image, video, audio, 3D and LLM workloads on every GPU generation we run.

• Set the model performance roadmap. Decide which models, hardware and techniques get the team's attention and in what order, based on real traffic, real cost and what the next generation of pods will run.

• Do the hardest work yourself: write and tune CUDA kernels, fuse attention and MLP paths, bring up new quantization formats (FP8, FP4, INT4) with quality held, and get new parallelism and batching strategies working on multi-GPU nodes.

• Make new models fast on day one. Build the pipeline that takes a newly released open model from weights to a production-grade, optimized deployment in days, and keep closing that gap.

• Choose and shape the serving stack: TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, SGLang, custom diffusion and video pipelines, and the Sonic Inference Engine's own runtime. Decide what we adopt, what we fork and what we write ourselves, and contribute upstream where it pays.

• Own the benchmarking and performance regression system: reproducible, hardware-aware measurement of throughput, latency, cost and quality for every model we serve, wired into CI so that a regression never reaches a pod.

• Partner with infrastructure and hardware engineering on GPU memory, storage and network bottlenecks that show up as inference latency, and feed what you learn back into the next generation of servers and pods.

• Build and lead the team. Hire principal and senior engineers, set the bar for technical rigour, mentor the people on the team, and run it so that a very small group delivers performance across a very large model catalogue.

• Deep, current, hands-on CUDA and GPU architecture expertise: kernel design, memory hierarchy and occupancy, Tensor Cores, fused kernels, CUDA Graphs, NCCL, and the profilers (Nsight Systems and Compute) that show exactly where a microsecond goes.

• Real production experience with at least one major inference engine (TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, SGLang or similar) and with the techniques that define modern serving: continuous batching, paged KV cache, speculative decoding, prefill/decode disaggregation, quantization and tensor, pipeline and expert parallelism.

• Fluent in Python and C++, comfortable in PyTorch internals, torch.compile and Triton, and happy to write the benchmark, the kernel and the CI job yourself rather than waiting for someone else to.

• Experience leading engineers: you have built or run a performance team, hired for it, set its technical direction and stayed hands-on while doing so.

Nice to have

• Diffusion and video generation performance: DiT and UNet pipelines, attention at long sequence lengths, step distillation, caching across denoising steps, LoRA hot-swapping, and the loaders and samplers in ComfyUI, Diffusers or custom engines.

• Contributions to TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, SGLang, FlashAttention, CUTLASS, Triton, Dynamo or similar open-source inference projects, or an open-source project of your own that people run.

title: Senior Staff Engineer - Infrastructure Systems
description:
As Senior Staff Engineer, Infrastructure Systems, you will own the GPU software stack on every Runware node: the firmware, the kernel and NVIDIA driver, the CUDA runtime and libraries, the container runtime, and the way Kubernetes and our inference services see and share a GPU. When a GPU misbehaves anywhere in the fleet, you will find out why and write the software that keeps it from happening again.

This is a senior staff-level individual contributor role for someone who knows GPUs from the driver up and still writes code every day. One month that means qualifying a new driver and CUDA release against every model family we serve. The next it is the GPU part of the acceptance suite that every node must pass, a detector that catches a failing GPU from its Xid and ECC history before a customer does, the bring-up of a new GPU generation, or a CUDA error that turns out to start in firmware, a PCIe link or a kernel update. You will work directly with the node operations, Managed Kubernetes, inference performance and Sonic Inference Engine teams, and be the person each of them calls when the problem sits below the framework.

Success means that every GPU in every pod runs a known, tested combination of firmware, driver and CUDA, that upgrades roll across the fleet without failed inferences, that GPU faults are detected, classified and remediated automatically, and that a new GPU generation goes from delivery to serving traffic in days.

What you'll do

• Own the GPU software baseline. Versioned, reproducible combinations of kernel, NVIDIA driver, firmware, CUDA runtime and libraries (cuDNN, cuBLAS, NCCL, TensorRT) and container toolkit, tested before they roll and rolled across the fleet without downtime.

• Qualify every driver and CUDA release. Keep the compatibility matrix across GPU generations, frameworks and model families, and catch regressions in correctness, performance and memory use before they reach production.

• Take GPU failures to root cause: Xid errors, CUDA "unknown error", cuBLAS handle failures, out-of-memory and fragmentation, GPUs that fall off the bus. Separate hardware, firmware, driver, runtime and application causes, and prove which one it is.

• Build GPU acceptance and diagnostics: the burn-in, DCGM diagnostics, memory and interconnect tests and real-workload tests that gate every node and rack before it serves traffic, and the reports customers receive at handover.

• Make GPU health visible and self-healing. Pull telemetry from DCGM, the driver, the kernel log and the BMC into one trusted view, classify faults, and automate the drain, reset and replacement paths.

• Own how GPUs are exposed to workloads: the container runtime, device plugins and the GPU Operator, MIG and sharing policies, and isolation between tenants, on bare metal and on Kubernetes.

• Bring up new GPU generations and new pods with the hardware and node operations teams: first driver and firmware, NVLink and NVSwitch validation, and the automation that makes the next bring-up take days.

We're a remote-first collective, meeting in person twice a year to plan, brainstorm, celebrate wins, and enjoy some face-to-face time. We have core hours for cooperative working and calls, but outside of that your calendar is yours. Work the hours that let you perform at your peak while also building a healthy life.

Our release cycles are fast and intense, but they're followed by real downtime. After big pushes we expect the team to unplug, recharge, and come back ready and stronger than ever for the next leap.

• Generous paid time off: vacation, sick days, public holidays

• Meaningful stock options: share in the upside you create

• Flexible hours: own your schedule outside core collaboration blocks

• Family leave: paid maternity, paternity, and caregiver time

• Company retreats: twice-yearly gatherings in inspiring locations
